1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh — _test_write_result defensive fallback (#626).
3	#
4	# Wave 10 defense-in-depth on top of #625. The writer must fail-CLOSED:
5	# test-results.json is ALWAYS written and ALWAYS parseable as JSON, even when
6	# callers pass adversarial input (whitespace in numeric slots, control chars in
7	# test_output, embedded quotes/backticks in test_cmd). When jq rejects the
8	# input, a degenerate-but-valid fallback object is written and a
9	# `test.result_write.fallback` event is emitted. jq stderr never leaks to the
10	# terminal.
11	set -uo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
14	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
15	
16	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
17	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
18	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
19	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
20	
21	print_test_header "test-plugin _test_write_result defensive fallback (#626)"
22	
23	setup_test_env "test-plugin-result-write-fallback"
24	
25	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
26	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
27	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
28	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
29	
30	ARTIFACT_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state/artifacts"
31	mkdir -p "$ARTIFACT_DIR"
32	
33	# shellcheck source=../../plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh
34	source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh"
35	
36	# ─── Helper: drive _test_write_result and assert basic invariants ─────────────
37	# Args: <label> <out_path> <stderr_path> -- <args-to-_test_write_result>
38	_drive_writer() {
39	    local label="$1"; shift
40	    local out="$1"; shift
41	    local err="$1"; shift
42	    [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && shift
43	    _test_write_result "$@" 2>"$err" || true
44	
45	    assert_file_exists "$label: results file written" "$out"
46	
47	    if jq empty "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
48	        assert_pass "$label: results file is valid JSON"
49	    else
50	        assert_fail "$label: results file is valid JSON" \
51	            "jq empty failed; content: $(head -c 200 "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
52	    fi
53	
54	    if grep -qiE 'jq: error|invalid (numeric literal|json|input)|Cannot iterate' "$err"; then
55	        assert_fail "$label: no jq error leaked to stderr" \
56	            "stderr: $(cat "$err")"
57	    else
58	        assert_pass "$label: no jq error leaked to stderr"
59	    fi
60	}
61	
62	# ─── 1. whitespace `passed` slot (adversarial numeric input) ────────────────
63	print_test_section "1. whitespace in passed slot triggers fallback"
64	
65	OUT1="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-ws-passed.json"
66	ERR1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ws-passed.stderr"
67	_drive_writer "ws-passed" "$OUT1" "$ERR1" -- \
68	    "$OUT1" "error" "broken" 0 "  " 0 "out" "false" "cmd" "bad_passed"
69	
70	# Sanitized passed should be null (not 0 — we don't silently coerce garbage).
71	assert_eq "ws-passed: .data.passed sanitized to null" "null" \
72	    "$(jq -r '.data.passed' "$OUT1" 2>/dev/null)"
73	
74	# ─── 2. non-numeric `failed` slot (`abc`) ────────────────────────────────────
75	print_test_section "2. non-numeric failed slot triggers sanitizer"
76	
77	OUT2="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-abc-failed.json"
78	ERR2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/abc-failed.stderr"
79	_drive_writer "abc-failed" "$OUT2" "$ERR2" -- \
80	    "$OUT2" "error" "broken" 0 0 "abc" "out" "false" "cmd" "bad_failed"
81	
82	assert_eq "abc-failed: .data.failed sanitized to null" "null" \
83	    "$(jq -r '.data.failed' "$OUT2" 2>/dev/null)"
84	
85	# ─── 3. control-char test_output ──────────────────────────────────────────────
86	print_test_section "3. control-char test_output is accepted, JSON still valid"
87	
88	OUT3="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-ctl.json"
89	ERR3="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ctl.stderr"
90	CTL_OUT=$'\x01\x02bad\x03'
91	_drive_writer "ctl-output" "$OUT3" "$ERR3" -- \
92	    "$OUT3" "error" "broken" 1 0 1 "$CTL_OUT" "false" "cmd"
93	
94	# ─── 4. embedded-quote test_cmd ───────────────────────────────────────────────
95	print_test_section "4. embedded quotes/backticks in test_cmd survive"
96	
97	OUT4="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-quotes.json"
98	ERR4="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/quotes.stderr"
99	EVIL_CMD='"npm" '\''test'\'' `evil`'
100	_drive_writer "quotes" "$OUT4" "$ERR4" -- \
101	    "$OUT4" "error" "broken" 1 0 1 "" "false" "$EVIL_CMD"
102	
103	# .data.test_cmd should round-trip verbatim through jq.
104	GOT_CMD="$(jq -r '.data.test_cmd' "$OUT4" 2>/dev/null)"
105	assert_eq "quotes: .test_cmd round-trips" "$EVIL_CMD" "$GOT_CMD"
106	
107	# ─── 5. non-bool diff_applied slot ────────────────────────────────────────────
108	print_test_section "5. non-bool diff_applied is sanitized to false"
109	
110	OUT5="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-bad-bool.json"
111	ERR5="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bad-bool.stderr"
112	_drive_writer "bad-bool" "$OUT5" "$ERR5" -- \
113	    "$OUT5" "error" "broken" 0 0 0 "out" "garbage" "cmd"
114	
115	assert_eq "bad-bool: .data.diff_applied sanitized to false" "false" \
116	    "$(jq -r '.data.diff_applied' "$OUT5" 2>/dev/null)"
117	
118	# ─── 6. whitespace exit_code slot ─────────────────────────────────────────────
119	print_test_section "6. whitespace exit_code is sanitized to null"
120	
121	OUT6="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-ws-ec.json"
122	ERR6="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ws-ec.stderr"
123	_drive_writer "ws-exit" "$OUT6" "$ERR6" -- \
124	    "$OUT6" "error" "broken" "  " 0 0 "" "false" "cmd"
125	
126	assert_eq "ws-exit: .data.exit_code sanitized to null" "null" \
127	    "$(jq -r '.data.exit_code' "$OUT6" 2>/dev/null)"
128	
129	# ─── 7. all-good happy path still works (no regression) ──────────────────────
130	print_test_section "7. happy path (no regression)"
131	
132	OUT7="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-happy.json"
133	ERR7="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/happy.stderr"
134	_drive_writer "happy" "$OUT7" "$ERR7" -- \
135	    "$OUT7" "pass" "complete" 0 5 0 "ok" "true" "npm test"
136	
137	assert_eq "happy: .verdict" "pass" "$(jq -r '.outcome' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
138	assert_eq "happy: .data.exit_code" "0" "$(jq -r '.data.exit_code' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
139	assert_eq "happy: .data.passed" "5" "$(jq -r '.data.passed' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
140	assert_eq "happy: .data.diff_applied" "true" "$(jq -r '.data.diff_applied' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
141	# [SPEC-11] run_mode at top level, pinned to its value AND agreeing with data.
142	# The value pin alone reddens at the v1 baseline; the data agreement is what
143	# catches a later regression that drops the top-level mirror.
144	_spec11_rm="$(jq '(.result_contract == 3) and (.run_mode == "full") and (.run_mode == .data.run_mode)' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
145	assert_eq "[SPEC-11] run_mode=full at top level, agreeing with data.run_mode" "true" "$_spec11_rm"
146	
147	# ─── 8. forced jq failure exercises the fallback branch + event emission ────
148	# Copilot P1 on #640: without this case the suite proved sanitization works
149	# but never actually walked the failure path. Shim jq via PATH so it exits 1
150	# unconditionally, which makes the real implementation hit the fallback
151	# writer and emit test.result_write.fallback.
152	print_test_section "8. forced jq failure: fallback JSON + event emitted"
153	
154	JQ_SHIM_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/jq-shim"
155	mkdir -p "$JQ_SHIM_DIR"
156	REAL_JQ="$(command -v jq)"
157	# Selectively fail only for the writer's `jq -n ...` invocation. Other
158	# callers (event-bus.sh, assertions, schema lookup) still get real jq so
159	# emit_event keeps working and the test can observe the fallback event.
160	cat > "$JQ_SHIM_DIR/jq" <<SHIM
161	#!/usr/bin/env bash
162	if [[ "\$1" == "-n" ]]; then
163	    exit 1
164	fi
165	exec "$REAL_JQ" "\$@"
166	SHIM
167	chmod +x "$JQ_SHIM_DIR/jq"
168	
169	OUT8="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-forced-fail.json"
170	ERR8="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/forced-fail.stderr"
171	
172	# event-bus.sh captured ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL at source-time (when plugin.sh
173	# loaded), so just truncate the existing file rather than re-pointing.
174	: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
175	
176	PATH="$JQ_SHIM_DIR:$PATH" _test_write_result \
177	    "$OUT8" "error" "broken" 0 0 0 "out" "false" "cmd" 2>"$ERR8" || true
178	
179	assert_file_exists "forced-fail: results file written" "$OUT8"
180	
181	if jq empty "$OUT8" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
182	    assert_pass "forced-fail: fallback JSON is parseable"
183	else
184	    assert_fail "forced-fail: fallback JSON is parseable" \
185	        "content: $(head -c 200 "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
186	fi
187	
188	assert_eq "forced-fail: .reason=result_write_failed" "result_write_failed" \
189	    "$(jq -r '.reason' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
190	assert_eq "forced-fail: .outcome=broken (#2366)" "broken" \
191	    "$(jq -r '.outcome' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
192	
193	# [SPEC-13] The fail-closed fallback is a v2 result too, in the SAME shape the
194	# normal path emits — not a v2-flavoured subset. A consumer cannot know which
195	# writer produced the artifact, so one that reads `.exit_code` at the top level
196	# must not silently get null just because the primary write failed.
197	assert_eq "[SPEC-13] fallback: .result_contract=3" "3" \
198	    "$(jq -r '.result_contract' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
199	assert_eq "[SPEC-13] fallback: .outcome=broken" "broken" \
200	    "$(jq -r '.outcome' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
201	assert_eq "[SPEC-13] fallback carries the same top-level mirrors as the normal path" "true" \
202	    "$(jq '(.test_output == .data.test_output) and (.run_mode == .data.run_mode) and (.exit_code == .data.exit_code)' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
203	
204	if grep -q '"type":"test.result_write.fallback"' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null; then

209	fi

213	# declared in the test plugin's manifest and composed into the known set — no
214	# longer in the engine's config/event-schema.json. Asserting against the
215	# manifest is the stronger statement: it pins the OWNER, not just membership.
216	print_test_section "9. test.result_write.fallback declared by the test plugin's manifest"
217	
218	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/event-bus/known-types.sh"
219	
220	# Here-strings, not pipes: `producer | grep -q` SIGPIPEs the producer under
221	# pipefail and turns a FOUND match into a failure (#1015, #1260).
222	if grep -qxF "test.result_write.fallback" \
223	        <<< "$(eb_manifest_events "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/manifest.yaml")"; then
224	    assert_pass "schema: test.result_write.fallback declared in provides.events"
225	else
226	    assert_fail "schema: test.result_write.fallback declared in provides.events" \
227	        "not present in plugins/tool/test/manifest.yaml::provides.events"
228	fi

231	    assert_pass "schema: test.result_write.fallback is in the composed known set"
232	else

234	        "composition (engine config + manifests) did not yield it"
235	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh — _test_write_result defensive fallback (#626).
#
# Wave 10 defense-in-depth on top of #625. The writer must fail-CLOSED:
# test-results.json is ALWAYS written and ALWAYS parseable as JSON, even when
# callers pass adversarial input (whitespace in numeric slots, control chars in
# test_output, embedded quotes/backticks in test_cmd). When jq rejects the
# input, a degenerate-but-valid fallback object is written and a
# `test.result_write.fallback` event is emitted. jq stderr never leaks to the
# terminal.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "test-plugin _test_write_result defensive fallback (#626)"

setup_test_env "test-plugin-result-write-fallback"

export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"

ARTIFACT_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state/artifacts"
mkdir -p "$ARTIFACT_DIR"

# shellcheck source=../../plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh"

# ─── Helper: drive _test_write_result and assert basic invariants ─────────────
# Args: <label> <out_path> <stderr_path> -- <args-to-_test_write_result>
_drive_writer() {
    local label="$1"; shift
    local out="$1"; shift
    local err="$1"; shift
    [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && shift
    _test_write_result "$@" 2>"$err" || true

    assert_file_exists "$label: results file written" "$out"

    if jq empty "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "$label: results file is valid JSON"
    else
        assert_fail "$label: results file is valid JSON" \
            "jq empty failed; content: $(head -c 200 "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
    fi

    if grep -qiE 'jq: error|invalid (numeric literal|json|input)|Cannot iterate' "$err"; then
        assert_fail "$label: no jq error leaked to stderr" \
            "stderr: $(cat "$err")"
    else
        assert_pass "$label: no jq error leaked to stderr"
    fi
}

# ─── 1. whitespace `passed` slot (adversarial numeric input) ────────────────
print_test_section "1. whitespace in passed slot triggers fallback"

OUT1="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-ws-passed.json"
ERR1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ws-passed.stderr"
_drive_writer "ws-passed" "$OUT1" "$ERR1" -- \
    "$OUT1" "error" "broken" 0 "  " 0 "out" "false" "cmd" "bad_passed"

# Sanitized passed should be null (not 0 — we don't silently coerce garbage).
assert_eq "ws-passed: .data.passed sanitized to null" "null" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.passed' "$OUT1" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── 2. non-numeric `failed` slot (`abc`) ────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "2. non-numeric failed slot triggers sanitizer"

OUT2="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-abc-failed.json"
ERR2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/abc-failed.stderr"
_drive_writer "abc-failed" "$OUT2" "$ERR2" -- \
    "$OUT2" "error" "broken" 0 0 "abc" "out" "false" "cmd" "bad_failed"

assert_eq "abc-failed: .data.failed sanitized to null" "null" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.failed' "$OUT2" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── 3. control-char test_output ──────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "3. control-char test_output is accepted, JSON still valid"

OUT3="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-ctl.json"
ERR3="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ctl.stderr"
CTL_OUT=$'\x01\x02bad\x03'
_drive_writer "ctl-output" "$OUT3" "$ERR3" -- \
    "$OUT3" "error" "broken" 1 0 1 "$CTL_OUT" "false" "cmd"

# ─── 4. embedded-quote test_cmd ───────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "4. embedded quotes/backticks in test_cmd survive"

OUT4="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-quotes.json"
ERR4="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/quotes.stderr"
EVIL_CMD='"npm" '\''test'\'' `evil`'
_drive_writer "quotes" "$OUT4" "$ERR4" -- \
    "$OUT4" "error" "broken" 1 0 1 "" "false" "$EVIL_CMD"

# .data.test_cmd should round-trip verbatim through jq.
GOT_CMD="$(jq -r '.data.test_cmd' "$OUT4" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "quotes: .test_cmd round-trips" "$EVIL_CMD" "$GOT_CMD"

# ─── 5. non-bool diff_applied slot ────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "5. non-bool diff_applied is sanitized to false"

OUT5="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-bad-bool.json"
ERR5="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bad-bool.stderr"
_drive_writer "bad-bool" "$OUT5" "$ERR5" -- \
    "$OUT5" "error" "broken" 0 0 0 "out" "garbage" "cmd"

assert_eq "bad-bool: .data.diff_applied sanitized to false" "false" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.diff_applied' "$OUT5" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── 6. whitespace exit_code slot ─────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "6. whitespace exit_code is sanitized to null"

OUT6="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-ws-ec.json"
ERR6="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ws-ec.stderr"
_drive_writer "ws-exit" "$OUT6" "$ERR6" -- \
    "$OUT6" "error" "broken" "  " 0 0 "" "false" "cmd"

assert_eq "ws-exit: .data.exit_code sanitized to null" "null" \
    "$(jq -r '.data.exit_code' "$OUT6" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── 7. all-good happy path still works (no regression) ──────────────────────
print_test_section "7. happy path (no regression)"

OUT7="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-happy.json"
ERR7="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/happy.stderr"
_drive_writer "happy" "$OUT7" "$ERR7" -- \
    "$OUT7" "pass" "complete" 0 5 0 "ok" "true" "npm test"

assert_eq "happy: .verdict" "pass" "$(jq -r '.outcome' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "happy: .data.exit_code" "0" "$(jq -r '.data.exit_code' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "happy: .data.passed" "5" "$(jq -r '.data.passed' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "happy: .data.diff_applied" "true" "$(jq -r '.data.diff_applied' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null)"
# [SPEC-11] run_mode at top level, pinned to its value AND agreeing with data.
# The value pin alone reddens at the v1 baseline; the data agreement is what
# catches a later regression that drops the top-level mirror.
_spec11_rm="$(jq '(.result_contract == 3) and (.run_mode == "full") and (.run_mode == .data.run_mode)' "$OUT7" 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
assert_eq "[SPEC-11] run_mode=full at top level, agreeing with data.run_mode" "true" "$_spec11_rm"

# ─── 8. forced jq failure exercises the fallback branch + event emission ────
# Copilot P1 on #640: without this case the suite proved sanitization works
# but never actually walked the failure path. Shim jq via PATH so it exits 1
# unconditionally, which makes the real implementation hit the fallback
# writer and emit test.result_write.fallback.
print_test_section "8. forced jq failure: fallback JSON + event emitted"

JQ_SHIM_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/jq-shim"
mkdir -p "$JQ_SHIM_DIR"
REAL_JQ="$(command -v jq)"
# Selectively fail only for the writer's `jq -n ...` invocation. Other
# callers (event-bus.sh, assertions, schema lookup) still get real jq so
# emit_event keeps working and the test can observe the fallback event.
cat > "$JQ_SHIM_DIR/jq" <<SHIM
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [[ "\$1" == "-n" ]]; then
    exit 1
fi
exec "$REAL_JQ" "\$@"
SHIM
chmod +x "$JQ_SHIM_DIR/jq"

OUT8="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-forced-fail.json"
ERR8="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/forced-fail.stderr"

# event-bus.sh captured ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL at source-time (when plugin.sh
# loaded), so just truncate the existing file rather than re-pointing.
: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"

PATH="$JQ_SHIM_DIR:$PATH" _test_write_result \
    "$OUT8" "error" "broken" 0 0 0 "out" "false" "cmd" 2>"$ERR8" || true

assert_file_exists "forced-fail: results file written" "$OUT8"

if jq empty "$OUT8" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "forced-fail: fallback JSON is parseable"
else
    assert_fail "forced-fail: fallback JSON is parseable" \
        "content: $(head -c 200 "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
fi

assert_eq "forced-fail: .reason=result_write_failed" "result_write_failed" \
    "$(jq -r '.reason' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "forced-fail: .outcome=broken (#2366)" "broken" \
    "$(jq -r '.outcome' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"

# [SPEC-13] The fail-closed fallback is a v2 result too, in the SAME shape the
# normal path emits — not a v2-flavoured subset. A consumer cannot know which
# writer produced the artifact, so one that reads `.exit_code` at the top level
# must not silently get null just because the primary write failed.
assert_eq "[SPEC-13] fallback: .result_contract=3" "3" \
    "$(jq -r '.result_contract' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "[SPEC-13] fallback: .outcome=broken" "broken" \
    "$(jq -r '.outcome' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null)"
assert_eq "[SPEC-13] fallback carries the same top-level mirrors as the normal path" "true" \
    "$(jq '(.test_output == .data.test_output) and (.run_mode == .data.run_mode) and (.exit_code == .data.exit_code)' "$OUT8" 2>/dev/null || echo false)"

if grep -q '"type":"test.result_write.fallback"' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "forced-fail: test.result_write.fallback event emitted"
else
    assert_fail "forced-fail: test.result_write.fallback event emitted" \
        "events.jsonl: $(cat "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null)"
fi

# ─── 9. schema registration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# #1717: `test.result_write.fallback` is the test plugin's OWN event, so it is
# declared in the test plugin's manifest and composed into the known set — no
# longer in the engine's config/event-schema.json. Asserting against the
# manifest is the stronger statement: it pins the OWNER, not just membership.
print_test_section "9. test.result_write.fallback declared by the test plugin's manifest"

source "$REPO_ROOT/core/event-bus/known-types.sh"

# Here-strings, not pipes: `producer | grep -q` SIGPIPEs the producer under
# pipefail and turns a FOUND match into a failure (#1015, #1260).
if grep -qxF "test.result_write.fallback" \
        <<< "$(eb_manifest_events "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/manifest.yaml")"; then
    assert_pass "schema: test.result_write.fallback declared in provides.events"
else
    assert_fail "schema: test.result_write.fallback declared in provides.events" \
        "not present in plugins/tool/test/manifest.yaml::provides.events"
fi

if grep -qxF "test.result_write.fallback" <<< "$(eb_compose_known_types)"; then
    assert_pass "schema: test.result_write.fallback is in the composed known set"
else
    assert_fail "schema: test.result_write.fallback is in the composed known set" \
        "composition (engine config + manifests) did not yield it"
fi

# ─── [#1754/SPEC-1] jq succeeds but primary atomic_write fails ───────────────
# Before #1754 only PIPESTATUS[0] (jq's exit) was captured.  When jq succeeded
# but atomic_write failed, _jq_rc stayed 0, stage_result_add silently merged
# the new outcome into the stale prior-round file, and the result came out as
# the (now-wrong) current outcome — the broken fallback never fired.
# After #1754 PIPESTATUS[1] (atomic_write) is captured too; a failed write sets
# _jq_rc non-zero and the broken fallback fires, writing outcome=broken +
# reason=result_write_failed, regardless of any prior-round file at the path.
print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-1] jq succeeds, primary atomic_write fails → broken fallback"

OUT_1754S1="$ARTIFACT_DIR/results-aw-fail-1754spec1.json"

# Write a prior-round pass result so stage_result_add has something to merge
# with before the fix — this confirms the bug was real (a stale file existed)
# and not a vacuous empty-file case.
stage_result_write "$OUT_1754S1" "pass" "prior round passed" 2>/dev/null || true

# Save the real atomic_write so the fallback path (calls #2, #3) can still
# succeed after the primary write is intercepted.
eval "$(declare -f atomic_write | sed 's/atomic_write ()/_aw_real_1754s1 ()/')"

_1754s1_aw_calls=0
atomic_write() {
    _1754s1_aw_calls=$(( _1754s1_aw_calls + 1 ))
    if [[ "$_1754s1_aw_calls" -eq 1 ]]; then
        # Primary write: drain stdin (prevents SIGPIPE on the jq producer), fail.
        cat > /dev/null
        return 1
    fi
    _aw_real_1754s1 "$@"
}

_test_write_result "$OUT_1754S1" "pass" "complete" 0 5 0 "ok" "true" "npm test" "" "full" \
    2>/dev/null || true

# Restore atomic_write so subsequent sections are unaffected.
eval "$(declare -f _aw_real_1754s1 | sed 's/_aw_real_1754s1 ()/atomic_write ()/')"

assert_file_exists "[#1754/SPEC-1] result file exists after fallback write" "$OUT_1754S1"

if jq empty "$OUT_1754S1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-1] fallback result is valid JSON"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-1] fallback result is valid JSON" \
        "content: $(head -c 200 "$OUT_1754S1" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
fi

assert_eq "[#1754/SPEC-1] primary write failure writes outcome=broken" "broken" \
    "$(jq -r '.outcome // empty' "$OUT_1754S1" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1754/SPEC-1] primary write failure writes reason=result_write_failed" "result_write_failed" \
    "$(jq -r '.reason // empty' "$OUT_1754S1" 2>/dev/null || true)"

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh — `reason` is mandatory in the result (#2050).
3	#
4	# test-results.json declares result_contract: 3. Since #1821 the reader treats a
5	# missing/empty `reason` as a STRUCTURAL failure and returns raw `error`
6	# (core/pipeline/verdict.sh:382-388,423) — which _cycle_detect_blocked halts on.
7	# So a red suite that omits `reason` is reported as a broken stage rather than a
8	# failing one, and build_test_cycle terminates `blocked` on iteration 1 instead
9	# of handing the failures back to build (run 33720837199).
10	#
11	# These SPECs drive the REAL writer into the REAL reader: whatever
12	# _test_write_result puts on disk is what runner_read_stage_verdict classifies,
13	# against the test plugin's own shipped manifest. No fixture stands in between.
14	set -uo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
17	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
18	
19	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
20	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
21	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
22	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
23	
24	print_test_header "test plugin — mandatory v2 reason (#2050)"
25	
26	setup_test_env "test-result-reason-contract"
27	
28	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
29	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
30	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
31	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
32	
33	# shellcheck source=../../core/event-bus/event-bus.sh
34	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
35	# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/verdict.sh
36	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/verdict.sh"
37	# shellcheck source=../../plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh
38	source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh"
39	# SPEC-8 drives the halt decision itself, so the predicate that ended run
40	# 33720837199 is the real one, not a restatement of it.
41	# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
42	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"
43	
44	STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
45	ART_DIR="$STATE_DIR/artifacts"
46	RESULT="$ART_DIR/test-results.json"
47	# The stage's own shipped manifest — the `${artifact_dir}` template, the
48	# `primary: true` marker and the declared type all come from the real file, so a
49	# manifest change that breaks this contract surfaces here too.
50	TEST_MANIFEST="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/manifest.yaml"
51	mkdir -p "$ART_DIR"
52	
53	_reason_of() { jq -r '.reason // ""' "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null || true; }
54	
55	# Classify the result currently on disk through the live reader. rc=0 so the
56	# `rc always wins` short-circuit cannot mask what the artifact says: a red suite
57	# reaches the cycle with rc=0 because the test plugin returns 0 and reports the
58	# failure through the verdict (plugin.sh:556).
59	_classify() { runner_read_stage_verdict "$STATE_DIR" "$TEST_MANIFEST" "test" 0; }
60	
61	# Count contract-violation events appended since line <from>. Always prints a
62	# number — an early `return` with no output would compare as "" and read as a
63	# failure regardless of what the engine did.
64	_violations_since() {
65	    local from="$1" n
66	    [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]] || { printf '0'; return 0; }
67	    n="$(tail -n "+$((from + 1))" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" \
68	        | grep -c 'stage.verdict.contract_violation')" || n=0
69	    printf '%s' "${n:-0}"
70	}
71	
72	_event_count() {
73	    [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]] || { printf '0'; return 0; }
74	    wc -l < "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" | tr -d ' '
75	}
76	
77	# ─── [SPEC-1] a plain failing suite ──────────────────────────────────────────
78	# The live shape from run 33720837199: parser recognized the runner, one test
79	# failed, no special-case reason applies. This is the arm that halted the cycle.
80	print_test_section "SPEC-1 — a red suite is a failing stage, not a broken one"
81	
82	rm -f "$RESULT"
83	_ev0="$(_event_count)"
84	_test_write_result "$RESULT" "fail" "complete" 1 670 1 \
85	    "unit 400/400 · e2e 7/8 · FAIL: e2e (exit 1)" "false" "npm test" "" "full"
86	
87	_r1="$(_reason_of)"
88	if [[ -n "$_r1" ]]; then
89	    assert_pass "[SPEC-1] failing suite writes a non-empty reason (got: $_r1)"
90	else
91	    assert_fail "[SPEC-1] failing suite writes a non-empty reason" \
92	        "reason absent or empty; result=$(cat "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null | head -c 200)"
93	fi
94	
95	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] the reader classifies a red suite as fail, not error" \
96	    "fail" "$(_classify)"
97	
98	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] no contract violation is emitted for a red suite" \
99	    "0" "$(_violations_since "$_ev0")"
100	
101	# ─── [SPEC-2] a passing suite ────────────────────────────────────────────────
102	# Same omission, same downgrade. It never halted a run only because the cycle
103	# evaluates convergence before _cycle_detect_blocked — the artifact is wrong on
104	# the green path too, and any consumer reading it directly sees `error`.
105	print_test_section "SPEC-2 — a green suite is a passing stage"
106	
107	rm -f "$RESULT"
108	_ev0="$(_event_count)"
109	_test_write_result "$RESULT" "pass" "complete" 0 671 0 \
110	    "unit 400/400 · integration 238/238" "false" "npm test" "" "full"
111	
112	_r2="$(_reason_of)"
113	if [[ -n "$_r2" ]]; then
114	    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] passing suite writes a non-empty reason (got: $_r2)"
115	else
116	    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] passing suite writes a non-empty reason" \
117	        "reason absent or empty; result=$(cat "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null | head -c 200)"
118	fi
119	
120	assert_eq "[SPEC-2] the reader classifies a green suite as pass" \
121	    "pass" "$(_classify)"
122	
123	assert_eq "[SPEC-2] no contract violation is emitted for a green suite" \
124	    "0" "$(_violations_since "$_ev0")"
125	
126	# ─── [SPEC-3] the derived reason states what the stage observed ──────────────
127	# ADR-054 §5: a result that cannot explain itself to an operator is incomplete.
128	# A placeholder token would satisfy the reader's presence check while telling an
129	# operator nothing, so the counts must survive into the reason.
130	print_test_section "SPEC-3 — the derived reason carries the counts"
131	
132	# Matched whole, not by substring: "1" alone occurs inside "671", so a
133	# substring check would still pass if the writer reported the wrong count.
134	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] a red suite's reason names failed-of-total" \
135	    "1 of 671 tests failed" "$_r1"
136	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] a green suite's reason names passed-of-total" \
137	    "671 of 671 tests passed" "$_r2"
138	
139	# ─── [SPEC-7] positive control — the detector this rests on actually fires ───

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh — `reason` is mandatory in the result (#2050).
#
# test-results.json declares result_contract: 3. Since #1821 the reader treats a
# missing/empty `reason` as a STRUCTURAL failure and returns raw `error`
# (core/pipeline/verdict.sh:382-388,423) — which _cycle_detect_blocked halts on.
# So a red suite that omits `reason` is reported as a broken stage rather than a
# failing one, and build_test_cycle terminates `blocked` on iteration 1 instead
# of handing the failures back to build (run 33720837199).
#
# These SPECs drive the REAL writer into the REAL reader: whatever
# _test_write_result puts on disk is what runner_read_stage_verdict classifies,
# against the test plugin's own shipped manifest. No fixture stands in between.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "test plugin — mandatory v2 reason (#2050)"

setup_test_env "test-result-reason-contract"

export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"

# shellcheck source=../../core/event-bus/event-bus.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/verdict.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/verdict.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh"
# SPEC-8 drives the halt decision itself, so the predicate that ended run
# 33720837199 is the real one, not a restatement of it.
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"

STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
ART_DIR="$STATE_DIR/artifacts"
RESULT="$ART_DIR/test-results.json"
# The stage's own shipped manifest — the `${artifact_dir}` template, the
# `primary: true` marker and the declared type all come from the real file, so a
# manifest change that breaks this contract surfaces here too.
TEST_MANIFEST="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/test/manifest.yaml"
mkdir -p "$ART_DIR"

_reason_of() { jq -r '.reason // ""' "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# Classify the result currently on disk through the live reader. rc=0 so the
# `rc always wins` short-circuit cannot mask what the artifact says: a red suite
# reaches the cycle with rc=0 because the test plugin returns 0 and reports the
# failure through the verdict (plugin.sh:556).
_classify() { runner_read_stage_verdict "$STATE_DIR" "$TEST_MANIFEST" "test" 0; }

# Count contract-violation events appended since line <from>. Always prints a
# number — an early `return` with no output would compare as "" and read as a
# failure regardless of what the engine did.
_violations_since() {
    local from="$1" n
    [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]] || { printf '0'; return 0; }
    n="$(tail -n "+$((from + 1))" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" \
        | grep -c 'stage.verdict.contract_violation')" || n=0
    printf '%s' "${n:-0}"
}

_event_count() {
    [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]] || { printf '0'; return 0; }
    wc -l < "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" | tr -d ' '
}

# ─── [SPEC-1] a plain failing suite ──────────────────────────────────────────
# The live shape from run 33720837199: parser recognized the runner, one test
# failed, no special-case reason applies. This is the arm that halted the cycle.
print_test_section "SPEC-1 — a red suite is a failing stage, not a broken one"

rm -f "$RESULT"
_ev0="$(_event_count)"
_test_write_result "$RESULT" "fail" "complete" 1 670 1 \
    "unit 400/400 · e2e 7/8 · FAIL: e2e (exit 1)" "false" "npm test" "" "full"

_r1="$(_reason_of)"
if [[ -n "$_r1" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-1] failing suite writes a non-empty reason (got: $_r1)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-1] failing suite writes a non-empty reason" \
        "reason absent or empty; result=$(cat "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null | head -c 200)"
fi

assert_eq "[SPEC-1] the reader classifies a red suite as fail, not error" \
    "fail" "$(_classify)"

assert_eq "[SPEC-1] no contract violation is emitted for a red suite" \
    "0" "$(_violations_since "$_ev0")"

# ─── [SPEC-2] a passing suite ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Same omission, same downgrade. It never halted a run only because the cycle
# evaluates convergence before _cycle_detect_blocked — the artifact is wrong on
# the green path too, and any consumer reading it directly sees `error`.
print_test_section "SPEC-2 — a green suite is a passing stage"

rm -f "$RESULT"
_ev0="$(_event_count)"
_test_write_result "$RESULT" "pass" "complete" 0 671 0 \
    "unit 400/400 · integration 238/238" "false" "npm test" "" "full"

_r2="$(_reason_of)"
if [[ -n "$_r2" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] passing suite writes a non-empty reason (got: $_r2)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] passing suite writes a non-empty reason" \
        "reason absent or empty; result=$(cat "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null | head -c 200)"
fi

assert_eq "[SPEC-2] the reader classifies a green suite as pass" \
    "pass" "$(_classify)"

assert_eq "[SPEC-2] no contract violation is emitted for a green suite" \
    "0" "$(_violations_since "$_ev0")"

# ─── [SPEC-3] the derived reason states what the stage observed ──────────────
# ADR-054 §5: a result that cannot explain itself to an operator is incomplete.
# A placeholder token would satisfy the reader's presence check while telling an
# operator nothing, so the counts must survive into the reason.
print_test_section "SPEC-3 — the derived reason carries the counts"

# Matched whole, not by substring: "1" alone occurs inside "671", so a
# substring check would still pass if the writer reported the wrong count.
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] a red suite's reason names failed-of-total" \
    "1 of 671 tests failed" "$_r1"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] a green suite's reason names passed-of-total" \
    "671 of 671 tests passed" "$_r2"

# ─── [SPEC-7] positive control — the detector this rests on actually fires ───
# SPEC-1/SPEC-2 assert an ABSENCE, which passes for free if the reader never
# emits or the counter never counts. Strip `reason` back off a conformant result
# and the violation must reappear, with the verdict downgraded to `error` — the
# exact pair observed in run 33720837199. Without this the green above is inert.
print_test_section "SPEC-7 — stripping the reason reproduces the halt"

_test_write_result "$RESULT" "fail" "complete" 1 670 1 \
    "some output" "false" "npm test" "" "full"
jq 'del(.reason)' "$RESULT" > "$RESULT.stripped" && mv "$RESULT.stripped" "$RESULT"

_ev0="$(_event_count)"
assert_eq "[SPEC-7] a result with no reason is classified error" \
    "error" "$(_classify)"
assert_eq "[SPEC-7] a result with no reason emits one contract violation" \
    "1" "$(_violations_since "$_ev0")"

# An empty-string reason is the same structural failure as an absent one — the
# reader checks length, so a writer that emitted `reason: ""` would satisfy a
# naive has() check and still halt the cycle.
jq '.reason = ""' "$RESULT" > "$RESULT.empty" && mv "$RESULT.empty" "$RESULT"
assert_eq "[SPEC-7] an empty-string reason is classified error too" \
    "error" "$(_classify)"

# ─── [SPEC-4 guard] explicit reasons are untouched ───────────────────────────
# #485 silent_failure and #584 summary_unavailable are the two reasons callers
# pass today (#2364 retired missing_diff_patch with the guard that wrote it). A default must not overwrite them.
print_test_section "SPEC-4 (guard) — an explicit reason still wins"

for _case in "silent_failure:error:broken:0:0:0" \
             "summary_unavailable:error:broken:1:null:null"; do
    IFS=':' read -r _want _v _d _rc _p _f <<< "$_case"
    rm -f "$RESULT"
    _test_write_result "$RESULT" "$_v" "$_d" "$_rc" "$_p" "$_f" \
        "" "false" "npm test" "$_want" "full"
    assert_eq "[SPEC-4 guard] explicit reason '$_want' is preserved verbatim" \
        "$_want" "$(_reason_of)"
done

# ─── [SPEC-5] adversarial input still yields a conformant result ─────────────
# #626's sanitizers absorb control chars, a non-boolean flag and a malformed
# timing blob, so the NORMAL writer runs — this is not the jq fallback branch
# (that one hardcodes reason=result_write_failed and is covered by
# test-plugin-result-write-fallback-test.sh:189). The point here is that the
# mandatory field survives the sanitizer path too, not only the clean one.
print_test_section "SPEC-5 — a sanitized write still carries a reason"

rm -f "$RESULT"
_test_write_result "$RESULT" "fail" "complete" 1 670 1 \
    "$(printf 'ctrl\x01chars')" "not-a-bool" 'weird `cmd` "quoted"' "" "full" \
    "{{{malformed" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if jq empty "$RESULT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] the result is valid JSON under adversarial input"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] the result is valid JSON under adversarial input" \
        "content: $(head -c 200 "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
fi

if [[ -n "$(_reason_of)" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a sanitized write carries a non-empty reason"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a sanitized write carries a non-empty reason" \
        "result=$(cat "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null | head -c 200)"
fi

# ─── [SPEC-6 guard] mandatory v2 fields are all present ──────────────────────
# The reader checks verdict, disposition and reason as one set. Assert the whole
# set so a future edit cannot fix `reason` by dropping a sibling.
print_test_section "SPEC-6 (guard) — every mandatory field is present (#2366: contract 3)"

rm -f "$RESULT"
_test_write_result "$RESULT" "fail" "complete" 1 670 1 \
    "some output" "false" "npm test" "" "full"

for _field in outcome reason; do
    if jq -e --arg f "$_field" \
        'has($f) and (.[$f] | type == "string") and (.[$f] | length > 0)' \
        "$RESULT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "[SPEC-6 guard] '$_field' is present and non-empty"
    else
        assert_fail "[SPEC-6 guard] '$_field' is present and non-empty" \
            "result=$(cat "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null | head -c 300)"
    fi
done

assert_eq "[SPEC-6 guard] result_contract is 3 (#2366)" \
    "3" "$(jq -r '.result_contract // ""' "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null || true)"

# ─── [SPEC-8] the whole chain: writer → reader → halt decision ───────────────
# The bug's consequence was never the JSON — it was build_test_cycle giving up
# on iteration 1. Run the real writer into the real reader into the real
# predicate and assert the cycle keeps iterating on a red suite. Both arms are
# asserted so the pass cannot come from a predicate that never fires.
print_test_section "SPEC-8 — a red suite lets the cycle iterate"

_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="test-2050"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_CYCLE_STAGES=(build test)
_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="pass"

# rc 0 = blocked (terminate now), rc 1 = not blocked (keep iterating).
_blocked_rc_for() {
    local verdict="$1" rc
    set +e
    _cycle_detect_blocked \
        "{\"build\":{\"verdict\":\"pass\"},\"test\":{\"verdict\":\"$verdict\"}}" 1
    rc=$?
    set +e
    printf '%s' "$rc"
}

rm -f "$RESULT"
_test_write_result "$RESULT" "fail" "complete" 1 670 1 \
    "unit 400/400 · e2e 7/8 · FAIL: e2e (exit 1)" "false" "npm test" "" "full"
assert_eq "[SPEC-8] a red suite does NOT block the cycle (rc=1, keep iterating)" \
    "1" "$(_blocked_rc_for "$(_classify)")"

# Negative control — the production failure, reproduced. Strip the field the
# writer now guarantees and the same chain terminates the cycle.
jq 'del(.reason)' "$RESULT" > "$RESULT.stripped" && mv "$RESULT.stripped" "$RESULT"
assert_eq "[SPEC-8] with no reason the same chain blocks (rc=0, run 33720837199)" \
    "0" "$(_blocked_rc_for "$(_classify)")"

# ─── [#1754/SPEC-2] reader classifies broken after primary atomic_write fails ─
# Before #1754: only PIPESTATUS[0] was captured in _test_write_result.  A
# failed atomic_write left the prior-round file untouched and stage_result_add
# merged the current outcome into it — so the reader saw "pass" (or whatever
# the current call supplied), never "broken".
# After #1754: the write exit is captured; a failed write triggers the fallback,
# which writes outcome=broken, so runner_read_stage_verdict returns "error"
# (the engine's classification for the broken outcome) — not the prior round's
# outcome.
print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-2] reader sees broken after primary atomic_write failure"

rm -f "$RESULT"
# Write a prior-round pass result using the engine's own writer so the data
# is exactly what the real write path produces (not hand-made).
stage_result_write "$RESULT" "pass" "prior round passed" 2>/dev/null || true

# Save the real atomic_write so the fallback write (call #2+) can succeed.
eval "$(declare -f atomic_write | sed 's/atomic_write ()/_aw_real_1754s2 ()/')"

_1754s2_aw_calls=0
atomic_write() {
    _1754s2_aw_calls=$(( _1754s2_aw_calls + 1 ))
    if [[ "$_1754s2_aw_calls" -eq 1 ]]; then
        # Primary path: drain stdin to prevent SIGPIPE on the jq producer, fail.
        cat > /dev/null
        return 1
    fi
    _aw_real_1754s2 "$@"
}

# Run the writer — same outcome as the prior round (pass) so the only thing
# distinguishing a correct from incorrect result is whether the file reflects
# the write FAILURE (broken) or the silently-merged stale content (pass).
_test_write_result "$RESULT" "pass" "complete" 0 5 0 "ok" "true" "npm test" "" "full" \
    2>/dev/null || true

# Restore atomic_write before calling the reader, which may call it too.
eval "$(declare -f _aw_real_1754s2 | sed 's/_aw_real_1754s2 ()/atomic_write ()/')"

# The reader must return "error" (the engine's classification for the broken
# outcome), NOT "pass" (which is what the prior-round stale file would give
# before the fix, since stage_result_add merged "pass" into it).
assert_eq "[#1754/SPEC-2] reader classifies primary-write failure as error (not prior pass)" \
    "error" "$(_classify)"

# Cross-check: the raw outcome in the file is "broken", not the prior round's.
assert_eq "[#1754/SPEC-2] file carries broken outcome after primary write failure" "broken" \
    "$(jq -r '.outcome // empty' "$RESULT" 2>/dev/null || true)"

print_test_results

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: plugins/agent/intake — the v2 result contract (#1837): manifest, the
# result file on every exit path, and the one word each way of stopping earns.
# Split from intake-test.sh (1,046 lines), which keeps goal capture, the gh
# fetch and the closed-issue gate.
#
# D1 [change] closed issue → misconfigured (nothing was down; the operator
#             chose a closed issue) — covered across a process boundary in
#             tests/integration/intake-refuse-on-closed-subprocess-test.sh
# D2 [change] a failed issue fetch with no --goal → unavailable: GitHub, a
#             service zBuild depends on, is not responding
# D3 [guard]  no goal and no issue → misconfigured
# D4 [change] a goal that sanitizes to nothing → misconfigured (the input is
#             empty; zBuild is not broken)
# D5          moved to the engine (#2367): tests/integration/engine-run-branch-test.sh E6
# D6 [change] the caller's own TERM handler is back after intake returns
# D7 [change] a result file that cannot be written is reported: rc 1 and a
#             message naming the file — never a silent pass with no result
# D8 [change] no fallback path: with no ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR intake writes no
#             result beside the state file, and says the engine gave it none
# D9 [change] intake's result writer takes the disposition as its THIRD
#             argument, like every other stage's, so the disposition-word lint
#             sees intake's words (it saw none)
# D10 [change] a signal after intake wrote its result leaves that result alone
#             (review: a graceful-drain TERM after the pass turned it into a failure)
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "plugin: intake — v2 result contract (#1837)"
setup_test_env "plugin-intake-result"
# shellcheck source=intake-test-lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/intake-test-lib.sh"
# The gh mock is only for the issue tests; intake here runs goal-first.
rm -f "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh"

# _disp — the outcome intake last wrote (#2366: contract 3 carries one word);
# _reason — its reason.
_disp()   { jq -r '.outcome // empty' "$ARTIFACT_DIR/intake-result.json" 2>/dev/null || true; }
_reason() { jq -r '.reason // empty' "$ARTIFACT_DIR/intake-result.json" 2>/dev/null || true; }
# _run_intake — runs intake with a clean result file; prints rc.
_run_intake() {
    rm -f "$ARTIFACT_DIR/intake-result.json"
    local rc=0
    intake_run "intake" "$STATE_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    printf '%s' "$rc"
}

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# #1837: v2 contract — acceptance assertions
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

_mf="$PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml"

# ─── SPEC-4 [change]: manifest declares provides.result_contract: 3 (#2366) ─
_s4_contract="$(yaml_get "$_mf" "provides.result_contract" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1837/SPEC-4] manifest provides.result_contract == 3" "3" "$_s4_contract"

# ─── SPEC-5 [change]: no per-stage verdict list (#2366) ──────────────────────
if grep -q 'valid_verdicts' "$_mf" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-5] a contract-3 manifest declares no valid_verdicts" "found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-5] a contract-3 manifest declares no valid_verdicts"
fi

# ─── SPEC-6 [change]: intake-result.json primary:true IN outputs; scope_manifest not ─
# Extract the outputs section first — the stanza must live under outputs, not elsewhere.
_s6_outputs="$(awk '
    /^outputs:/ { in_s=1; next }
    in_s && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ && !/^outputs:/ { exit }
    in_s { print }
' "$_mf" 2>/dev/null || true)"

_s6_ir_stanza="$(awk '
    /intake.result|intake_result|intake-result/ { found=1 }
    found && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:/ && !/intake.result|intake_result|intake-result/ { exit }
    found { print }
' <<< "$_s6_outputs" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if grep -q 'primary: true' <<< "$_s6_ir_stanza"; then
    assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-6] intake-result.json is in outputs section with primary: true"
else
    assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-6] intake-result.json must declare primary: true within the outputs section" \
        "${_s6_outputs:-(outputs section absent)}"
fi

_s6_sm_stanza="$(awk '
    /scope.manifest|scope_manifest/ { found=1 }
    found && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:/ && !/scope.manifest|scope_manifest/ { exit }
    found { print }
' <<< "$_s6_outputs" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if grep -q 'primary: true' <<< "$_s6_sm_stanza"; then
    assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-6] scope_manifest must NOT have primary: true after migration" "found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-6] scope_manifest does not have primary: true"
fi

# ─── SPEC-7 [change]: manifest declares config.router.timeout_s and max_turns ─
# manifest_router_knob is loaded via registry.sh → manifest-validation.sh
_s7_timeout="$(manifest_router_knob "$_mf" timeout_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
_s7_maxturns="$(manifest_router_knob "$_mf" max_turns 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$_s7_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-7] manifest declares config.router.timeout_s"
else
    assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-7] manifest must declare config.router.timeout_s" "absent"
fi
if [[ -n "$_s7_maxturns" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-7] manifest declares config.router.max_turns"
else
    assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-7] manifest must declare config.router.max_turns" "absent"
fi

# ─── SPEC-8 [change]: scope-manifest.md and intake.md byte-identical to v1 golden ─
_s8_scope_golden="$REPO_ROOT/tests/golden/intake-scope-manifest-v1.golden"
_s8_goal_golden="$REPO_ROOT/tests/golden/intake-goal-v1.golden"
if [[ -f "$_s8_scope_golden" && -f "$_s8_goal_golden" ]]; then
    cat > "$STATE_DIR/platforms.json" <<'JSON'
{"detected":["ios","node"],"repo_head_sha":"golden"}
JSON
    export ZBUILD_GOAL="golden-parity: verify v1 intake content is preserved"
    rm -f "$STATE_DIR/scope-manifest.md" "$STATE_DIR/intake.md"
    set +e
    intake_run "intake" "$STATE_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1
    set -e
    if cmp -s "$STATE_DIR/scope-manifest.md" "$_s8_scope_golden"; then
        assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-8] scope-manifest.md is byte-identical to v1 golden"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-8] scope-manifest.md must match v1 golden fixture" \
            "run: diff $STATE_DIR/scope-manifest.md $_s8_scope_golden"
    fi
    if cmp -s "$STATE_DIR/intake.md" "$_s8_goal_golden"; then
        assert_pass "[#1837/SPEC-8] intake.md is byte-identical to v1 golden"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-8] intake.md must match v1 golden fixture" \
            "run: diff $STATE_DIR/intake.md $_s8_goal_golden"
    fi
else
    assert_fail "[#1837/SPEC-8] v1 golden fixtures must exist before migration" \
        "missing: intake-scope-manifest-v1.golden and/or intake-goal-v1.golden"
fi
rm -f "$STATE_DIR/platforms.json"

# ─── SPEC-2 [change]: intake-result.json written on every exit path ──────────
# Success path: run with a known goal and no issue
rm -f "$ARTIFACT_DIR/intake-result.json"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: every manifest-declared `primary: true` output is written through
3	# atomic_write in the plugin's plugin.sh. Grep-based static check (#507).
4	set -euo pipefail
5	
6	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
7	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
8	
9	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
10	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
11	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
12	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
13	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh
14	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh"
15	
16	print_test_header "primary-output atomicity guard (#507)"
17	
18	# Extract the basename of a manifest path (e.g. "${artifact_dir}/x.json" -> "x.json")
19	_basename_path() {
20	    local p="$1"
21	    p="${p##*/}"
22	    printf '%s' "$p"
23	}
24	
25	shopt -s nullglob
26	checked=0
27	violations=0
28	for manifest in "$REPO_ROOT"/plugins/*/*/manifest.yaml; do
29	    plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
30	    plugin_sh="$plugin_dir/plugin.sh"
31	    [[ -f "$plugin_sh" ]] || continue
32	
33	    row="$(manifest_graph_primary_output "$manifest" 2>/dev/null || true)"
34	    [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
35	    IFS='|' read -r p_id p_type _ p_req p_path <<< "$row"
36	    [[ -z "$p_path" ]] && continue
37	    base="$(_basename_path "$p_path")"
38	    [[ -z "$base" ]] && continue
39	
40	    checked=$((checked + 1))
41	
42	    # Accept any of:
43	    #   (a) direct: `atomic_write "...<base>..."` literal
44	    #   (b) indirect-via-var: `atomic_write "$..."` invocation AND the
45	    #       basename appears literally somewhere in the file
46	    #   (c) indirect-via-var + suffix: `atomic_write "$..."` AND the basename's
47	    #       trailing word (e.g. "findings.json") appears — covers manifests
48	    #       whose path interpolates a prefix (security${infix}-findings.json).
49	    #   (d) stage_result_write / stage_result_add AND the basename appears (#2366)
50	    # Search plugin.sh AND lib/*.sh (decomposed plugins store logic in lib/).
51	    base_suffix="${base#*-}"  # strip leading "prefix-" if present
52	    # shellcheck disable=SC2207
53	    plugin_srcs=("$plugin_sh")
54	    # shellcheck disable=SC2206
55	    if compgen -G "$plugin_dir/lib/*.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
56	        plugin_srcs+=( "$plugin_dir"/lib/*.sh )
57	    fi
58	    if grep -E "atomic_write[^|]*${base//./\\.}" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base written via atomic_write"
60	    elif grep -E '^[^#]*stage_result_(write|add)[[:space:]]' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
61	        && grep -F "$base" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	        # #2366: the one result writer (scripts/lib/stage-result.sh) writes via atomic_write.
63	        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base written via stage_result_write (atomic)"
64	    elif grep -E 'atomic_write[[:space:]]+"\$' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
65	        && grep -F "$base" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
66	        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base (indirect atomic_write reference)"
67	    elif grep -E 'atomic_write[[:space:]]+"\$' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
68	        && [[ -n "$base_suffix" && "$base_suffix" != "$base" ]] \
69	        && grep -F "$base_suffix" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
70	        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base (indirect via *-${base_suffix})"
71	    elif grep -E 'stage_result_(write|add)[[:space:]]' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
72	        && grep -F "$base" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
73	        # #2366: the one result writer writes through atomic_write.
74	        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base (via stage_result_write)"
75	    else
76	        assert_fail "$plugin_dir: primary $base NOT written via atomic_write" \
77	            "see ${plugin_sh#$REPO_ROOT/}"
78	        violations=$((violations + 1))
79	    fi
80	done

82	if [[ $checked -eq 0 ]]; then
83	    assert_fail "no primary outputs found across plugins" "manifest scan returned 0"
84	fi

86	# ─── [#1754/SPEC-5] lint-atomic-write-unchecked detects a bare | atomic_write ─
87	# Before #1754: scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh does not exist.
88	# After #1754: it exists and exits non-zero with the violating line in its output
89	# when given a .sh file that pipes to atomic_write without an error check.

91	
92	_LINT_SCRIPT="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh"
93	_SPEC5_FIXTURE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5-unchecked.sh"
94	cat > "$_SPEC5_FIXTURE" <<'FIXTURE'
95	#!/usr/bin/env bash
96	set -euo pipefail
97	_write_it() {
98	    printf '%s\n' "hello" | atomic_write "/some/output/path"
99	}
100	FIXTURE
101	
102	_spec5_rc=0
103	_spec5_out="$(bash "$_LINT_SCRIPT" "$_SPEC5_FIXTURE" 2>&1)" || _spec5_rc=$?
104	
105	if [[ "$_spec5_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
106	    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint exits non-zero for unchecked atomic_write"
107	else
108	    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint exits non-zero for unchecked atomic_write" \
109	        "exit code was 0; output: $_spec5_out"
110	fi
111	
112	# The output must name the violating line by number (e.g. :4 or file:4:text).
113	# Matching the filename alone is not sufficient — the line itself must be identified.
114	if grep -qE ':[0-9]+' <<< "$_spec5_out"; then
115	    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint names the violating line in its output"
116	else
117	    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint names the violating line in its output" \
118	        "output: $_spec5_out"
119	fi
120	
121	# ─── [#1754/SPEC-6] lint exits 0 for properly-checked atomic_write calls ──────
122	# The lint script must not flag calls whose exit is checked on the same or next
123	# physical line via &&, ||, if !, or PIPESTATUS that includes the write index.
124	print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-6] lint exits 0 when every atomic_write call is checked"
125	
126	_SPEC6_FIXTURE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec6-checked.sh"
127	cat > "$_SPEC6_FIXTURE" <<'FIXTURE'
128	#!/usr/bin/env bash
129	set -euo pipefail
130	# Same-line || check.
131	printf '%s\n' "hello" | atomic_write "/path/a" || exit 1
132	# Same-line && check.
133	printf '%s\n' "world" | atomic_write "/path/b" && echo ok
134	# Next-line || true annotation.
135	printf '%s\n' "aux" | atomic_write "/path/c" \
136	    || true
137	# PIPESTATUS capturing the write index.
138	printf '%s\n' "data" | atomic_write "/path/d"
139	local _aw_rc="${PIPESTATUS[1]}"
140	# if ! check.
141	if ! printf '%s\n' "val" | atomic_write "/path/e"; then echo "failed"; fi
142	FIXTURE
143	
144	_spec6_rc=0
145	_spec6_out="$(bash "$_LINT_SCRIPT" "$_SPEC6_FIXTURE" 2>&1)" || _spec6_rc=$?
146	
147	assert_eq "[#1754/SPEC-6] lint exits 0 for properly-checked calls" "0" "$_spec6_rc"
148	
149	# ─── [#1754/SPEC-7] package.json lint target invokes lint-atomic-write-unchecked ─
150	# The lint script is wired into `npm run lint` so CI enforces it on every PR.
151	print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-7] package.json lint target contains lint-atomic-write-unchecked"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: every manifest-declared `primary: true` output is written through
# atomic_write in the plugin's plugin.sh. Grep-based static check (#507).
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh"

print_test_header "primary-output atomicity guard (#507)"

# Extract the basename of a manifest path (e.g. "${artifact_dir}/x.json" -> "x.json")
_basename_path() {
    local p="$1"
    p="${p##*/}"
    printf '%s' "$p"
}

shopt -s nullglob
checked=0
violations=0
for manifest in "$REPO_ROOT"/plugins/*/*/manifest.yaml; do
    plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
    plugin_sh="$plugin_dir/plugin.sh"
    [[ -f "$plugin_sh" ]] || continue

    row="$(manifest_graph_primary_output "$manifest" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
    IFS='|' read -r p_id p_type _ p_req p_path <<< "$row"
    [[ -z "$p_path" ]] && continue
    base="$(_basename_path "$p_path")"
    [[ -z "$base" ]] && continue

    checked=$((checked + 1))

    # Accept any of:
    #   (a) direct: `atomic_write "...<base>..."` literal
    #   (b) indirect-via-var: `atomic_write "$..."` invocation AND the
    #       basename appears literally somewhere in the file
    #   (c) indirect-via-var + suffix: `atomic_write "$..."` AND the basename's
    #       trailing word (e.g. "findings.json") appears — covers manifests
    #       whose path interpolates a prefix (security${infix}-findings.json).
    #   (d) stage_result_write / stage_result_add AND the basename appears (#2366)
    # Search plugin.sh AND lib/*.sh (decomposed plugins store logic in lib/).
    base_suffix="${base#*-}"  # strip leading "prefix-" if present
    # shellcheck disable=SC2207
    plugin_srcs=("$plugin_sh")
    # shellcheck disable=SC2206
    if compgen -G "$plugin_dir/lib/*.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_srcs+=( "$plugin_dir"/lib/*.sh )
    fi
    if grep -E "atomic_write[^|]*${base//./\\.}" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base written via atomic_write"
    elif grep -E '^[^#]*stage_result_(write|add)[[:space:]]' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        && grep -F "$base" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # #2366: the one result writer (scripts/lib/stage-result.sh) writes via atomic_write.
        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base written via stage_result_write (atomic)"
    elif grep -E 'atomic_write[[:space:]]+"\$' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        && grep -F "$base" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base (indirect atomic_write reference)"
    elif grep -E 'atomic_write[[:space:]]+"\$' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        && [[ -n "$base_suffix" && "$base_suffix" != "$base" ]] \
        && grep -F "$base_suffix" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base (indirect via *-${base_suffix})"
    elif grep -E 'stage_result_(write|add)[[:space:]]' "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        && grep -F "$base" "${plugin_srcs[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # #2366: the one result writer writes through atomic_write.
        assert_pass "$plugin_dir: primary $base (via stage_result_write)"
    else
        assert_fail "$plugin_dir: primary $base NOT written via atomic_write" \
            "see ${plugin_sh#$REPO_ROOT/}"
        violations=$((violations + 1))
    fi
done

if [[ $checked -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_fail "no primary outputs found across plugins" "manifest scan returned 0"
fi

# ─── [#1754/SPEC-5] lint-atomic-write-unchecked detects a bare | atomic_write ─
# Before #1754: scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh does not exist.
# After #1754: it exists and exits non-zero with the violating line in its output
# when given a .sh file that pipes to atomic_write without an error check.
print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint-atomic-write-unchecked exits non-zero for unchecked call"

_LINT_SCRIPT="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh"
_SPEC5_FIXTURE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5-unchecked.sh"
cat > "$_SPEC5_FIXTURE" <<'FIXTURE'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
_write_it() {
    printf '%s\n' "hello" | atomic_write "/some/output/path"
}
FIXTURE

_spec5_rc=0
_spec5_out="$(bash "$_LINT_SCRIPT" "$_SPEC5_FIXTURE" 2>&1)" || _spec5_rc=$?

if [[ "$_spec5_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint exits non-zero for unchecked atomic_write"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint exits non-zero for unchecked atomic_write" \
        "exit code was 0; output: $_spec5_out"
fi

# The output must name the violating line by number (e.g. :4 or file:4:text).
# Matching the filename alone is not sufficient — the line itself must be identified.
if grep -qE ':[0-9]+' <<< "$_spec5_out"; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint names the violating line in its output"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-5] lint names the violating line in its output" \
        "output: $_spec5_out"
fi

# ─── [#1754/SPEC-6] lint exits 0 for properly-checked atomic_write calls ──────
# The lint script must not flag calls whose exit is checked on the same or next
# physical line via &&, ||, if !, or PIPESTATUS that includes the write index.
print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-6] lint exits 0 when every atomic_write call is checked"

_SPEC6_FIXTURE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec6-checked.sh"
cat > "$_SPEC6_FIXTURE" <<'FIXTURE'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Same-line || check.
printf '%s\n' "hello" | atomic_write "/path/a" || exit 1
# Same-line && check.
printf '%s\n' "world" | atomic_write "/path/b" && echo ok
# Next-line || true annotation.
printf '%s\n' "aux" | atomic_write "/path/c" \
    || true
# PIPESTATUS capturing the write index.
printf '%s\n' "data" | atomic_write "/path/d"
local _aw_rc="${PIPESTATUS[1]}"
# if ! check.
if ! printf '%s\n' "val" | atomic_write "/path/e"; then echo "failed"; fi
FIXTURE

_spec6_rc=0
_spec6_out="$(bash "$_LINT_SCRIPT" "$_SPEC6_FIXTURE" 2>&1)" || _spec6_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1754/SPEC-6] lint exits 0 for properly-checked calls" "0" "$_spec6_rc"

# ─── [#1754/SPEC-7] package.json lint target invokes lint-atomic-write-unchecked ─
# The lint script is wired into `npm run lint` so CI enforces it on every PR.
print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-7] package.json lint target contains lint-atomic-write-unchecked"

_PACKAGE_JSON="$REPO_ROOT/package.json"
if grep -q 'bash scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh' "$_PACKAGE_JSON" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-7] package.json lint target contains bash scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-7] package.json lint target must contain bash scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh" \
        "not found in $REPO_ROOT/package.json"
fi

# ─── [#1754/SPEC-8] lint exits 0 on the full codebase ─────────────────────────
# All 13 pre-existing unchecked | atomic_write sites outside the two bugs carry
# || true, so the lint passes on the real code tree.  This spec need not fail
# before the change; it must pass after.
print_test_section "[#1754/SPEC-8] lint-atomic-write-unchecked exits 0 on the full codebase"

_spec8_rc=0
_spec8_out="$(bash "$_LINT_SCRIPT" 2>&1)" || _spec8_rc=$?

if [[ "$_spec8_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-8] lint exits 0 on core/ plugins/ scripts/"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-8] lint exits 0 on core/ plugins/ scripts/" \
        "exit $_spec8_rc; output: ${_spec8_out:0:400}"
fi

# Verify the || true mechanism: outside the two bug-fix files that receive proper
# error handling, every | atomic_write call in core/ plugins/ scripts/ must carry
# || true on the same line (or be a shell continuation line whose next physical
# line carries || true).  This distinguishes "annotated" from "removed" or
# "silenced by a different mechanism".
_s8_grep_out="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s8-grep.txt"
grep -rn '| atomic_write' \
    "$REPO_ROOT/core" "$REPO_ROOT/plugins" "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" \
    --include='*.sh' 2>/dev/null > "$_s8_grep_out" || true

_s8_call_count=0
_s8_violations=()

while IFS= read -r _s8_entry; do
    _s8_f="${_s8_entry%%:*}"
    _s8_rest="${_s8_entry#*:}"
    _s8_lno="${_s8_rest%%:*}"
    _s8_text="${_s8_rest#*:}"
    # Exclude the two files fixed by #1754 (they get proper PIPESTATUS handling)
    [[ "$_s8_f" == */plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh ]] && continue
    [[ "$_s8_f" == */plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh ]] && continue
    # Exclude test directories (unit, integration, plugin-local)
    [[ "$_s8_f" == */tests/* ]] && continue
    # Exclude the lint script itself (it contains | atomic_write as a grep pattern)
    [[ "$_s8_f" == */lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh ]] && continue
    # A continuation line (ends with \) carries || true on the next physical line — OK
    grep -qE '\\[[:space:]]*$' <<< "$_s8_text" && continue
    _s8_call_count=$((_s8_call_count + 1))
    grep -qE '\|\|[[:space:]]*true' <<< "$_s8_text" || \
        _s8_violations+=("${_s8_f}:${_s8_lno}")
done < "$_s8_grep_out"

# The calls must still exist in the codebase — they must be annotated, not removed.
if [[ "$_s8_call_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-8] | atomic_write calls still present outside bug-fix files (not removed)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-8] | atomic_write calls still present outside bug-fix files (not removed)" \
        "found 0 calls in core/plugins/scripts outside exclusions"
fi

# Every remaining call must carry || true — the specified annotation mechanism.
if [[ "${#_s8_violations[@]}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1754/SPEC-8] all pre-existing | atomic_write calls outside bug-fix files carry || true"
else
    assert_fail "[#1754/SPEC-8] all pre-existing | atomic_write calls outside bug-fix files carry || true" \
        "missing || true at: ${_s8_violations[*]}"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

            elif [[ "$p" =~ ^[a-z0-9_-]+$ ]]; then
                printf '+ %s/\n' "$p"
            else
                warn "intake_run: skipping invalid platform id: $p"
            fi
        done
    } | atomic_write "$state_dir/scope-manifest.md"
    local _sm_aw_rc="${PIPESTATUS[1]}"
    if (( _sm_aw_rc != 0 )); then
        _intake_write_result "$_art" "broken" \
            "failed to write scope-manifest.md" || true
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$sanitized" | atomic_write "$state_dir/intake.md"
    local _im_aw_rc="${PIPESTATUS[1]}"
    if (( _im_aw_rc != 0 )); then
        _intake_write_result "$_art" "broken" \
            "failed to write intake.md" || true
        return 1
    fi

    local _title_line
    _title_line="${sanitized%%$'\n'*}"

    # #2306 (ADR-070 §1): the issue's requirements, numbered by the engine.
    if [[ -n "$fetched_ok" && -n "$_art" ]] && ! _intake_write_requirements "$_art" "$_raw_json"; then
        warn "intake_run: could not write $_art/requirements.json — later stages judge the issue text alone"
    fi

    # #2364: the result carries the issue text, so a later stage finds it by
    # what it is (data.issue_text), never by intake's file name.
    _intake_write_result "$_art" "pass" \
        "took in the goal for issue #$issue: ${_title_line:0:60}" \
        "$(jq -nc --arg t "$sanitized" --argjson n "${#platforms[@]}" \
            '{goal_len: ($t | length), platform_count: $n, issue_text: $t}')" || return 1
    stage_summary_write "${_intake_art:+$_intake_art/intake-summary.md}" "intake" "pass" \
        "took in the goal for issue #$issue: ${_title_line:0:60}" \
        "$(printf -- '- goal length: %s chars\n- platforms: %s' "${#sanitized}" "${#platforms[@]}")"
    emit_event "plugin.result" "plugin=intake" \
        "goal_len=${#sanitized}" \
        "platform_count=${#platforms[@]}"
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh — detect unchecked | atomic_write calls.
#
# A bare pipe to atomic_write whose exit is not checked lets a failed write
# pass silently, leaving the prior round's file looking current. This lint
# flags each violation: the same line or the immediately following executable
# line (blank and comment-only lines are skipped because comments do not reset
# PIPESTATUS in bash) must check the write exit via &&, ||, if !, or a
# PIPESTATUS capture that includes the write index.
#
# A shell-continuation line (ending with \) is checked together with its
# immediately following physical line for || or &&.
#
# Usage: bash scripts/lib/lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh [file...]
#   No args: scans core/ plugins/ scripts/ under the repo root.
# Exit 0: no violations. Exit 1: violations emitted as file:line: text.

set -uo pipefail

_law_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_law_root="$(cd "$_law_dir/../.." && pwd)"

# Collect files to scan
_law_files=()
if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
    _law_files=("$@")
else
    while IFS= read -r _law_f; do
        [[ -n "$_law_f" ]] && _law_files+=("$_law_f")
    done < <(find "$_law_root/core" "$_law_root/plugins" "$_law_root/scripts" \
        -name '*.sh' -type f 2>/dev/null | sort)
fi

_law_violations=0
# The pipe-to-write pattern, split across two variables so this script does
# not match its own patterns when scanned as part of the full codebase.
_law_pipe='|'
_law_fn='atomic_write'

for _law_file in "${_law_files[@]}"; do
    [[ -f "$_law_file" ]] || continue
    # Skip this lint script itself (it references the pattern in variable form)
    [[ "$_law_file" == */lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh ]] && continue

    mapfile -t _law_lines < "$_law_file"
    _law_n="${#_law_lines[@]}"

    for (( _law_i=0; _law_i<_law_n; _law_i++ )); do
        _law_line="${_law_lines[$_law_i]}"
        _law_lno=$(( _law_i + 1 ))

        # Skip comment-only lines (leading whitespace then #): they are not code
        grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#' <<< "$_law_line" && continue

        # Fast path: skip lines that do not contain the pipe-to-write token
        grep -qF "${_law_pipe} ${_law_fn}" <<< "$_law_line" || continue

        # Skip lines where the token appears only inside a single-quoted string
        # (e.g. assert_fail "... '| atomic_write' ..."): not executable code.
        # Strip every '...' span and check whether the token survives.
        _law_stripped="${_law_line}"
        while grep -qE "'" <<< "$_law_stripped"; do
            _before="${_law_stripped%%\'*}"
            _after="${_law_stripped#*\'}"
            _after="${_after#*\'}"
            _law_stripped="${_before}${_after}"
        done
        grep -qF "${_law_pipe} ${_law_fn}" <<< "$_law_stripped" || continue

        # 1. Same-line check: &&, ||, or if ! on the same line as the write
        grep -qE '(&&|\|\||if[[:space:]]+!)' <<< "$_law_line" && continue

        # 2. Continuation (\): current line ends with \; check next physical
        #    line for || or && (e.g. "... | atomic_write ... \ \n    || true")
        if grep -qE '\\[[:space:]]*$' <<< "$_law_line"; then
            _law_next_phys="${_law_lines[$(( _law_i + 1 ))]:-}"
            grep -qE '(\|\||&&)' <<< "$_law_next_phys" && continue
        fi

        # 3. Next executable line check: skip blank and comment-only lines
        #    (they do not reset PIPESTATUS), then look for a PIPESTATUS capture
        #    that includes the write index (e.g. PIPESTATUS[1]).
        _law_j=$(( _law_i + 1 ))
        _law_pstat=0
        while [[ "$_law_j" -lt "$_law_n" ]]; do
            _law_nxt="${_law_lines[$_law_j]}"
            # Blank or comment-only line: skip (does not reset PIPESTATUS)
            if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$' <<< "$_law_nxt"; then
                _law_j=$(( _law_j + 1 ))
                continue
            fi
            # First executable line: check for PIPESTATUS capture
            grep -qE 'PIPESTATUS\[' <<< "$_law_nxt" && _law_pstat=1
            break
        done
        [[ "$_law_pstat" -eq 1 ]] && continue

        # No exit check found: violation
        printf '%s:%d: %s\n' "$_law_file" "$_law_lno" "$_law_line"
        _law_violations=$(( _law_violations + 1 ))
    done
done

[[ "$_law_violations" -eq 0 ]]
